resale_co.name: Resale inspection (Residential Resale / Rental Inspection)
resale_co.issued_by: Construction & Code Enforcement (Code Enforcement / Housing Official)
resale_co.lead_time: Inspections are done on Fridays only
requirements: Yard free of debris and weeds and sheds empty; waterfront lots: bulkhead in good condition, fill maintained on the landward side, no floatable debris around or under the house
Home clean and move-in ready: trash, debris and hazardous material removed; paint, flooring, siding, roofing, windows and screens in good condition

Attached garage: 1/2 inch drywall on walls next to living space and on attic ceilings; two layers of type X drywall under living space above the garage; metal or rated doors in separation walls, including attic access
Stairs with graspable handrails and closed risers; decks and landings 30 inches or more above grade need 36 inch guardrails with openings under 4 inches
Smoke detectors to code (at least one per level in older homes and one within 10 feet of each bedroom) and CO detector within 10 feet of all bedrooms
Anti-tip device on the range
Electrical: no exposed wires, panel labeled, all boxes covered
Plumbing: water heater relief valve piped to within 6 inches of the floor; heating equipment properly vented
House numbers at least 4 inches near the front door (not on the door) and contrasting
Well water test by the Board of Health (if on a well)
Flood elevation certificate in a special flood hazard area
Chimney caps on all fireplaces; chimney, woodstove, fireplace and heat and hot water certificates from professionals
Lead paint certificate if built before 1978; bulkhead certificate (waterfront)
Portable fire extinguisher, minimum 2A:10BC, 2.5 to 10 lb dry chemical, within 10 feet of the kitchen
No sleeping space on the third floor in Tuckerton Meadows or in second-floor loft areas in Bartletts Landing
resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Borough's Rental/Resale Application packet (check 'Resale Inspection', give closing date and access or lock box instructions), attach the required professional certifications (well and septic, chimneys, woodstoves, fireplaces, heat and hot water, elevation, and lead paint for homes built before 1978), and submit it to Construction & Code Enforcement, 420 East Main Street (609-296-4916). Cash, check or money order only. Inspections are Fridays only.

resale_co.notes: Tuckerton's 2026 Rental/Resale packet combines the fire certificate application (page 1), the smoke/CO requirements (page 2), a resale or rental inspection application (page 3) and Code Enforcement's 21-item 'Residential Resale / Rental Inspection Checklist' (page 4), so a housing inspection on resale is part of the process. The ordinance itself was not viewed (ecode360). The only fee schedule in the packet ($75 / $150 / $225, non-refundable) is stated for the fire certificate inspection (see fire certificate); the packet does not say whether the resale housing checklist has a separate fee, and page 3 has a blank 'Re-inspection Fee' line. The packet is a scanned image; quotes were read from the page images. The Borough web page links Joe Ventresca's name to the Technical Assistant's address (LCranmer@TuckertonBorough.com, Lindsay Cranmer, Technical Assistant to Construction Officials), so no personal email is listed for him. Other contacts: Code Enforcement Officer and Deputy Zoning Officer James McAndrew (JMCANDREW@TuckertonBorough.com, 609-296-3254).

requirements: Smoke detectors on each level and outside each sleeping area near the bedrooms; hardwired or interconnected alarms required by year built: 1979 to 1981 hardwired outside sleeping areas; 1981 to 1987 hardwired outside sleeping areas and in the basement; 1987 to 1991 hardwired interconnected on each level; 1991 to present hardwired interconnected with battery backup in all bedrooms, outside each sleeping area and on every level

Since January 1, 2019 battery smoke alarms must be 10-year sealed units; all non-sealed battery detectors must be replaced; hardwired alarms from original construction may not be replaced with battery alarms
Smoke detectors not within 3 feet of a kitchen or bathroom, not within 20 feet of a flame-producing device, and not within 4 inches of a corner or lower than 12 inches from the ceiling on a wall
CO alarm within 10 feet of the sleeping areas
Portable fire extinguisher still on the May 2026 Borough form: minimum 2A:10BC, 2.5 to 10 lb dry chemical, within 10 feet of the kitchen

fire_cert.notes: The July 2026 LEA registry lists the NJ DCA Division of Fire Safety (S) as Tuckerton's fire code enforcing agency, but the DCA's list of state-enforced towns (revised 7/17/2026) shows 'TUCKERTON 1532' without the 'SC' (smoke certs) mark, and the Borough's own 2026 Rental/Resale packet has the Borough's Fire Prevention office issue the smoke/CO certificate. So sellers use the Borough, not the DCA online portal. Tuckerton has no separate page in the state fire directory. The Borough's fees ($75 / $150 / $225) are higher than the state DCA schedule. The form still requires a fire extinguisher although P.L.2025, c.19 removed it from the state requirement; it also does not mention the new secondary power source label.

other_items.label: Professional certifications
other_items.detail: Attach well and septic (well water test by the Board of Health), chimney, woodstove, fireplace, heat and hot water, elevation, and lead paint (homes built before 1978) certifications, all done by professionals.

other_items.label: Bulkhead certificate (waterfront)
other_items.detail: The resale checklist lists a bulkhead certificate and bulkhead condition for waterfront lots.

open_questions: Whether the resale housing inspection has its own fee separate from the $75 / $150 / $225 fire certificate fee, and the re-inspection fee amount.
How long the resale approval and fire certificate stay valid.
